newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks close mixed, no surprises expected.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks close mixed, no surprises expected.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed mixed on Friday as business slowed down with only top shares trading on higher volumes and analysts predicted no big changes on the market due to the beginning of the peak holiday season.
"Still, I believe that some trading will happen due to cheap prices of some stocks," said Davor Relja of Factor brokerage.
Four of 15 traded issues rose, five fell and six were flat. Volume and turnover were halved at 16,455 units and 16.1 million kuna, respectively. Total weekly turnover was 82.5 million kuna.
Drugs firm Pliva was the most actively traded issue with 5,522 shares sold. It was closely followed by another fully-listed stock, Zagrebacka Banka with 5,025 units traded.
Both stocks rose -- Pliva added ten kuna to 510 and while the price of Zagrebacka's shares edged up 16 kuna to 2,111.
"We are not expecting any big changes in the prices of either of these two market heavyweights in the coming week. We have to wait and see what happens next on the London Stock Exchange," Relja said.
Traders earlier ascribed their rise in prices and heavy trade to the strong dollar.
Pliva's GDRs continued to rise in London on Friday, fetching $16.075 by mid-afternoon, after opening at $15.9. Zagrebacka's GDRs were also higher at $33.7, up from the opening at $33.625.
Ship repairer Viktor Lenac was the top gainer rising 26 kuna to end at 155 kuna on volume of 1,000 shares.
One trader said this latest sharp rise in just two days of trading might be somewhat unrealistic, but added that the price was still expected to rise in the coming days.
Viktor Lenac this week became the fourth issue listed in the top bracket of the central bourse.
Another fully-listed stock, Varazdinska Banka A-series, traded flat at 210 kuna, selling 1,379 units.
Biggest decliner brewery Karlovacka Pivovara lost 30 kuna or 5.6 percent to 510 with 700 shares sold.
"The Karlovacka Pivovara situation is just an expected sequence of events that came after last week's euphoria and it may drop to 500 per share next week," said Relja.
Karlovacka was the market's favourite in the past weeks and some traders were predicting it would reach 600 kuna.
Food processor Podravka was flat at 245 kuna, selling 907 shares.
